subject: Post-demo: clarify performance commitments, multi-region routing, and data residency
messages:
From: Alice Torres <alice.torres@vectorpay.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 17:23:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: demo today — performance and residency questions

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the throughput/latency examples helpful. Before we write up next steps internally, two quick clarifying questions that came up from engineering and security: 

1) Latency targets: We need an organized summary of achievable p95/p99 latency for short-form (<=64 tokens) and long-form (>=512 tokens) streaming use cases across US/EU/APAC. We heard about fallback model variants — what are typical latency deltas when failing over to a smaller quantized variant?

2) Throughput & concurrency: For a peak traffic pattern of 120 reqs/s with 4 concurrent streams per request, what throughput profile and concurrency limits should we plan for? Any recommended headroom/burst guidance?

3) Regional routing & residency: Legal needs confirmation that EU traffic will be served from EU nodes by default and that data (prompts + KV cache) from EU sessions will remain in-region unless we explicitly route otherwise. For APAC we may accept eventual consistency but need estimated egress patterns.

4) Attachments: Please attach an SLO matrix or sketch of options we can present to finance/procurement.

If you can send a short post-call note with the numbers and a proposed next-step (tech call vs. contract review), that would be ideal.

— Alice
Product Lead, VectorPay

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Torres <alice.torres@vectorpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo today — performance and residency questions

Alice — great to meet you and the team today. See answers below and attached a concise SLO options workbook we use for commercial discussions. I also looped in Sean (account) to coordinate pricing/next steps.

Summary answers (high level):
- Latency (p95/p99):
  - Short-form (<=64 tokens): p95 ~35–60ms (US/EU), p99 ~70–120ms. APAC p95 ~60–90ms depending on region; p99 ~130–250ms.
  - Long-form (>=512 tokens) streaming: p95 ~120–220ms per token at sustained output; p99 can spike 2–3x under full-concurrency bursts.
- Fallback model delta: switching to a smaller 8-bit-quantized variant typically adds +15–40ms at p95 for short-form, and +30–70ms for streaming heavy requests, depending on sequence length.
- Throughput & concurrency guidance: for 120 reqs/s with 4 concurrent streams (480 concurrent streams), recommend Reserved capacity tier with autoscale buffer to 600 concurrent streams. Plan for 25% headroom for spikes (target 750 concurrent).
- Regional routing/data residency: EU traffic can be pinned to our EU region (Ireland/Frankfurt) with KV cache and prefix cache kept in-region. APAC routing can default to nearest APAC region but we can offer a stricter in-region residency contract for regulated data if required.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions eng) to validate perf numbers against your LLM usage profile.
2) Sean to share proposed commercial guardrails (commits/term).
3) If legal wants to confirm residency language, we can supply a short appendix on data flows and KMS integration.

Attached: Redwood_SLO_Options_Q32026.xlsx (SLO tiers + sizing), regional-routing-diagram.png (simple diagram).

Are you available for a 45-min tech call on Wed or Thu this week?

Thanks,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:01:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: demo today — performance and residency questions

Folks — forwarding Alice's follow-up and my quick answers (see thread). Can you help with verification and any changes to the SLO workbook before I send formally to VectorPay legal/eng?

Specific asks:
- Marissa: can you run a quick sim or cite a recent benchmark for a 120 rps (4 streams each) pattern — looking for expected p95/p99 on our committed Dedicated configuration and an estimate for the smaller quantized fallback? Please include memory / GPU footprint notes so I can justify the headroom.
- Sean: once we confirm numbers, I want to present three pricing options (starter reserved, committed baseline, and enterprise resilient) with associated latency guarantees and overage rules.

I plan to send a polished summary to VectorPay by end of day Tue (your timezone).

Thanks — Hannah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: demo today — performance and residency questions

Hannah / Sean — quick technical confirmation after a short run against our perf harness:

1) Benchmarks (Dedicated-reserved pool, n1-high-capacity config):
   - Short-form (<=64 tokens): p95 = 40ms (US/EU), p99 = 95ms. APAC p95=75ms p99=170ms.
   - Long-form (>=512 tokens streaming): steady-state per-token latency p95=160ms, p99=360ms when at 85–100% concurrency.

2) Quantized fallback (8-bit int8 variant):
   - Short-form delta: +22ms p95; p99 delta +35–60ms depending on GPU kernel availability.
   - Streaming delta: +45–90ms per token under heavy concurrency.

3) Throughput: for 120 req/s with 4 streams (480 concurrent streams) our measurements show Dedicated reserve with 4 x A100-like instances (autoscale headroom to 6) handles steady traffic with p95 targets preserved. Recommend a committed baseline with autoscale to cover 25–35% burst headroom (target 700–750 concurrent).

4) Data residency: default routing rules are region-aware; to guarantee in-region storage (prompts + KV cache) we enable an in-region strict residency policy and KMS key binding — we'll document the data flow. Note that cross-region failover is opt-in and would be listed in the appendix for legal.

Attached a small workbook tab where I added the specific numbers (sheet: VectorPay_Benchmarks). Also attached a quick regional routing SVG.

If this looks good I can prepare a one-page tech annex with the diagrams and numbers for legal review.

— Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Torres <alice.torres@vectorpay.com>

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 21:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarify performance commitments, multi-region routing, and data residency

Thanks — that level of detail is perfect. Two quick clarifications before we schedule procurement/legal reviews: 

- Can you add the p95/p99 numbers for a typical 256-token mid-length case in the workbook? Our UX team is most concerned about mid-length streaming latency.
- For APAC: we will probably accept eventual in-region caching for now but need explicit language on the maximum cross-region egress windows and whether KMS keys can be scoped per-region.

Assuming those two small updates, I'm happy to move this to a procurement intake and share the tech annex with our legal counsel. Proposed next step: 45-min tech deep dive on Thu 14:00 PT (I will invite our infra lead and legal). Sean — can you prepare the three commercial options Hannah mentioned?

We look forward to the annex and the short residency appendix.

— Alice
Product Lead, VectorPay
